title: The speculative archaeologist
content:
Esin Karaosman, currently a Visiting PhD students at Linnaeus University, gave a research seminar entitled “‘We Are All (Speculative) Archaeologists’, Archaeological Imagination in the Making of Alternative Futures” for ten researchers attending the Higher Seminar in Cultural Sciences at Linnaeus University in Kalmar (24 November 2026).

She described the content of her presentation with these words:

How can an architect become a speculative archaeologist, conducting field research at the edge of knowledge and imagination? Archaeology has developed a way of knowing shaped by its encounters with material remains, where the instability, loss, and transformation of knowledge make imagination necessary. The presentation will explore “speculative archaeology” by reorienting this “archaeological imagination” toward alternative presents and futures. By treating knowing as a form of speculation, and therefore as a design problem, Esin investigates how we can stage encounters with what could be otherwise. She asks: If “we are all archaeologists,” can we also become speculative archaeologists in the making of alternative futures?
